items.title: Daughter of Bondi attack victim describes impact of antisemitic hate online
items.description: The Jewish community's experiences of antisemitism has been put on display on the first day of the royal commission triggered by the Bondi Beach terror attack last year.

items.title: Kumanjayi Little Baby remembered across NT after 'unthinkable trauma'
items.description: The Northern Territory is continuing to grieve the short life of a five-year-old girl today, with crowds in Alice Springs to pay tribute by donning pink — her favourite colour.

items.title: Tax windfall from Iran war to be pocketed in federal budget
items.description: The extra tax revenue generated by the Iran war will be saved in its entirety, as the government downplays major cost-of-living relief in next week's federal budget — though the treasurer warns those gains will be small.

items.title: Live: Iran says Trump's plan to support ships through strait would violate ceasefire
items.description: A senior Iranian official says any US attempt to interfere in the Strait of Hormuz would violate the ceasefire after Donald Trump says the US will try to free up ships there. Follow live.

items.title: Live: Albanese heralds 'deep friendship' with Japan following meeting with Takaichi
items.description: Australia and Japan sign agreements on critical minerals, energy security and defence cooperation following a meeting between Anthony Albanese and Takaichi Sanae. Follow live.

items.title: Three die after suspected hantavirus outbreak on cruise ship
items.description: A suspected outbreak of hantavirus, which is spread by contact with rat and mice faeces, has killed three people on a cruise ship.

items.title: A hacker built a tool to track police officers. Then he tried to warn them
items.description: A security flaw means the location of devices used by police, potentially including undercover officers and those travelling home, is visible to anyone with a phone or laptop.

items.title: Daughter hopes $1m reward will solve mystery of mother's disappearance
items.description: Marion Barter has not been seen since 1997. Her daughter is determined to find out what happened to her mother, who she believes may have found herself "in a situation she did not fully control".

items.title: Australian businesses falling victim to new type of fraud
items.description: Higher inflation, a war in the Middle East, and a ban on surcharges are crippling small businesses. Now they are falling victim to a modern crime.

items.title: A new poll tells us a lot about One Nation's new-found support
items.description: A new poll asks Australians specifically about One Nation and the results show that rather than being a flash in the pan, the minor party's freight train may be a more lasting phenomenon.

items.title: Cultural practices harder to do with price of fuel in remote Australia
items.description: Cultural obligations and essential services are being impacted by the cost of fuel in Australia's most remote communities.

items.title: Busloads of tourists turn quiet street into 'internet sensation'
items.description: For years, the residents of Tasman Drive in Gerringong knew they lived in a stunningly beautiful part of the world, but then social media discovered it too.

items.title: Cold chips and lost remotes among reasons for 'absurd' Triple Zero calls
items.description: Triple Zero call centres are seeing an increase in "absurd" calls, ranging from lost television remote controls to ducks crossing the road.

items.title: It was a record race time. Moments later spectators were suspicious
items.description: Tasmania's top horse race was run 37 metres shorter than advertised. Officials knew the track distance was likely incorrect but proceeded anyway. This is what happened.

items.title: Four tasty and affordable rice dishes for busy weeknights
items.description: Rice doesn't need to play second fiddle. The cheap and simple pantry staple can hold up a whole meal.

items.title: Tim Roth battles Radha Mitchell in gripping Australian action flick
items.description: Shooting in snake-and-spider-infested grass on a Queensland farm, Seven Snipers spooked its stars.

items.title: Quiz: Can you name the typo on the $50 note?
items.description: Take a trip back in time with this week's history quiz.

items.title: China accused of targeting Port Pirie and Hobart metal smelters
items.description: South Australia's treasurer and energy minister says China is undermining Australia's smelting industry and that any shutdown would leave national security "very exposed".

items.title: 'Motivation to swim faster': Four people bitten by crocodile before swimming race
items.description: Four people were bitten by a suspected freshwater crocodile just a day before a sold-out swimming competition was run in the same far-north Western Australia lake.

items.title: Trump's former personal lawyer Rudy Giuliani in critical condition
items.description: Former New York mayor and US President Donald Trump's former personal lawyer Rudy Giuliani is in hospital in a critical condition.

items.title: Traffic gridlock as park visitors turn out to see the turning of the fagus
items.description: Nature lovers who went to see the autumn colours of the fagus at Tasmania's Mt Field National Park on Saturday say there were no car spaces and nowhere to turn around.

items.title: We're headed into an AI fog as the automation arms race begins
items.description: Artificial intelligence might be driving growth for data centre companies, but society is unprepared for the long-term risks posed to the rest of us.

items.title: Police search properties 32 years after teenager's disappearance
items.description: Gordana Kotevski was last seen in 1994 when witnesses saw the 16-year-old being forced into a vehicle by at least two people near Newcastle.

items.title: Quick hits: Gasly flips out, Verstappen spins and F1 could go back to V8s
items.description: Formula 1 returned from a five-week hiatus and made up for lost time in Miami. Here are the quick hits from the Formula 1 Miami Grand Prix.

items.title: Saifiti medically retires from league due to shoulder issue
items.description: Daniel Saifiti's stellar career with the Dolphins, Newcastle, NSW, and Fiji comes to a premature end due to injury.
